units.translation: where Blomfield rightly reads πτολίπορθ' [sacker of cities]. For although the tragedians did not use πτόλις [city] for πόλις [city] except when the meter demanded it, yet in the Homeric word πτολίπορθος [sacker of cities] Aeschylus undoubtedly preserved the Homeric form even without metrical necessity. There are no other examples of the form πτολιπόρθης [sacker of cities] except the proper name of Penelope's son in Pausanias 8, 12, 6.

which the scholiast explains as ὁ ὑπὸ Πυθοῦς χρησθείς Ορέστης [Orestes, who was prophesied by Pytho]. The ending is wrongly assimilated to another noun. It should be written πυθόχρηστος [sent by the Pythian oracle]. Thus Euripides Ion 1218 ὁ πυθόχρηστος Λοξίου νεανίας [the young man sent by Loxias' oracle], and Plutarch Moralia p. 163 b. πυθόχρηστον τῆς ἀποικίας ἡγεμόνα [a leader of the colony sent by the oracle].
